verdict.expected_speedup: 4–8× on 8-core CPU at N=128; 50–200× on GPU at N≥2048
verdict.justification: The double-buffered stencil is embarrassingly parallel within each sweep, making OpenMP collapse(2) a natural and low-overhead fit; at N=128 the grid fits in L2 cache so shared-memory threading avoids DRAM bandwidth limits entirely. CUDA becomes superior only at larger N where the working set exceeds the LLC and GPU memory bandwidth dominates. MPI is a poor fit because the 2 KB per-sweep halo exchange cost vastly exceeds the per-rank compute at this problem size.
